description: The mechanisms, other than the OPA rules themselves, that count as an automated method for a Key Security Indicator (FRC-CSX-VVK), each with what it tests and how scripts/build-sdr.py verifies its result before counting it. An OPA rule counts for a KSI through its own annotations (custom.ksi_ids and custom.resource_types), never through this table. A mechanism counts once per KSI however many records it publishes. Read by scripts/_ksi_methods.py, which fails closed on a missing or malformed file.
rationale: The mechanisms are those the 2026-11-06 strict review judged to genuinely test a KSI's measures (the plan the operator approved on 2026-11-06 names them: the audit-log review; the recovery exercise's rebuild-and-compare and its versioning and point-in-time-recovery read; Grype and Dependabot as separate detectors; runtime divergence; reconcile (a); Checkov/tfsec and the live security settings; the plan-gate run and the conformance results; the inbox simulation; training, as one mechanism; CodeQL and ZAP with their clocks; and availability.json). Which KSIs each covers follows the same review's per-KSI table. No mechanism was added to reach a count. AI-drafted; the measure sentences and KSI lists are for the operator's review. input is 'stand-in' where the mechanism runs on a labelled stand-in (synthetic messages, a simulated trainee): it still counts as a method, and a KSI that reaches two methods only with it is Simulated, not Implemented. 2026-11-06 (night), by the operator's choice of the drills plan (not to satisfy a gate): the significant-change evaluation log, the Annual Security Review, the Board of Sam, the CFO's budget review, the incident pattern review, the after-action lessons check, the Choose-Your-Own-Disaster tabletop, the disclosure drill, the security.txt check and the phishing drill, and the recovery rebuild for KSI-RPL-ARP. Every stand-in method states its stand_in_proof. AI-drafted, for the operator's review. Version 2026-11-06.3 adds three live drills the operator chose on 2026-11-06 (the quarantine responder's nightly drill, the monthly Chaos Gremlin restore drill and availability incidents measured against the recovery time objective), each run on schedule, and adds KSI-IAM-SUS to the audit-log review, whose reportable findings now start the responder. AI-drafted, for the operator's review.

methods.mechanism: Nightly audit-log review (scripts/audit-log-review.py)
methods.measure: Every CloudTrail write event and every GitHub change to main, workflows, rulesets and environments since the previous review is judged by rule, a planted simulated intruder must be caught on every run, and a write evaluated reportable that names an IAM user or role starts the quarantine responder against it.

methods.mechanism: Monthly recovery exercise, rebuild and compare (scripts/hold-recovery-exercise.py, check a)
methods.measure: The live site is rebuilt from the deployed commit and compared byte for byte with what is served.

methods.mechanism: Monthly recovery exercise, versioning and point-in-time recovery read (scripts/hold-recovery-exercise.py, check b)
methods.measure: Versioning on every bucket and point-in-time recovery on the state-lock table are re-read from the verified runtime signal.

methods.mechanism: Grype dependency scanning (the VDR's detection feed)
methods.measure: Every npm and PyPI package in this inventory's Syft SBOM is scanned against a fresh vulnerability database, and the scan passes the detection gate.

methods.mechanism: Dependabot alerts (the VDR's detection feed)
methods.measure: GitHub's dependency advisories for this repository are read on every VDR build and pass the detection gate.

methods.mechanism: CodeQL code scanning with its clock (the VDR's detection feed)
methods.measure: Every required CodeQL category was analysed on main without error inside its 72-hour window, and its open alerts enter the VDR with remediation clocks.

methods.mechanism: OWASP ZAP authenticated API scan with its clock (the VDR's detection feed)
methods.measure: The authenticated dynamic scan of the Silk Reeling API reached its target inside its 72-hour window, and its alerts enter the VDR with remediation clocks.

methods.mechanism: Checkov and tfsec infrastructure-as-code scanning (the VDR's detection feeds)
methods.measure: The Terraform is scanned against the cloud provider's published best-practice checks, and both scans pass the detection gate.

methods.mechanism: Live security settings compared with the Secure Configuration Guide (scripts/check-secure-config.py)
methods.measure: Every security setting of the top-level administrative and privileged accounts is read live and matches the guide's recommended default or an accepted deviation.

methods.mechanism: Runtime divergence (the runtime emitter's comparison with the deploy-time signal)
methods.measure: The daily runtime re-validation finds no KSI the deploy published as passing failing against the live account.

methods.mechanism: Reconciliation invariant (a) (scripts/reconcile.py)
methods.measure: Every live in-boundary resource is in the inventory: nothing exists outside configuration management.

methods.mechanism: The deploy's OPA plan gate run (the signed KSI signal)
methods.measure: Every change is validated against the policy before it is applied, on every deploy, and the run is signed.

methods.mechanism: The method's conformance suite (scripts/build-conformance.py)
methods.measure: Every conformance test the method profile maps runs and passes before the deploy proceeds.

methods.mechanism: FedRAMP Security Inbox simulation (scripts/build-fsi-simulation.py)
methods.measure: The inbox and incident-paging procedure runs over committed synthetic messages and every outcome matches the expected one.

replaceable.statement: A real inbox would feed received messages to the same scripts/_fsi.py logic in place of data/fsi-simulation/messages.json; the mail transport and the recorded-not-sent outbound legs are what would change.

methods.mechanism: Training currency and completion (scripts/_training.py)
methods.measure: The training packet generated from the system's own data is current, and the current packet was completed by its due date with a passing score and a steady trend, by a simulated trainee.

replaceable.statement: A real trainee's quiz answers would replace scripts/_training.py take() as the input to the same currency and completion checks; only the answer source changes.

methods.mechanism: Independent availability measurement (scripts/build-availability.py)
methods.measure: The service's availability is measured from outside it and the measurement is current.

methods.mechanism: Significant-change evaluation log (scripts/build-scn.py, SCN-CSO-MAR)
methods.measure: Every change merged to main carries a valid significant-change evaluation, appended to a signed log that a deploy cannot rewrite, and none is logged with a problem.

methods.mechanism: Annual Security Review (scripts/hold-security-review.py)
methods.measure: Each year the review is generated from the system's data (documents and their checks, new component types against the threat model, decisions, findings and incident patterns, recurring cost) and fails on any failing item; only the reviewer's sign-off is simulated.

replaceable.statement: A real reviewer would sign off the same generated review in place of Rev Yewer (simulated); the checks and their inputs are already real, so only the signOff entries would change.

methods.mechanism: The Board of Sam, quarterly (scripts/hold-drill.py, scripts/_drills.py board_meeting)
methods.measure: Every in-force risk acceptance in the decision register is endorsed at a meeting held on or after the day it was decided, the board refuses one past its review date, and a planted acceptance left off the agenda is found unendorsed.

replaceable.statement: Real executives' endorsements would replace endorse(), recorded in the same endorsements list; endorsement_gaps() and the published check would not change.

methods.mechanism: The CFO's quarterly budget review (scripts/hold-drill.py, scripts/_drills.py cfo_review)
methods.measure: Every automated method in this table is funded by a line of data/recurring-costs.json and the known recurring cost is within the stated ceiling; a planted unfunded mechanism is refused.

methods.mechanism: Groundhog Day: incident pattern review (scripts/_incidents.py patterns(), published in the incident log)
methods.measure: Real incidents of the last 12 months are grouped by root cause and component, a pattern seen twice opens a VDR process finding, and a seeded scenario of three identical incidents is flagged on every build.

replaceable.statement: The register holds only exercises today, which patterns() excludes, so the seeded scenario is what it runs on; a real incident recorded in data/incidents.json with its pattern is grouped by the same function with no change.

methods.mechanism: After-action lessons check (scripts/_incidents.py lessons_check(), published in the incident log)
methods.measure: Every resolved incident has lessons learned, each linking to a commit, decision or test that exists, and a planted orphan lesson is caught on every build.

replaceable.statement: The resolved incidents in the register are exercises today; a real incident's lessons are checked by the same function with no change.

methods.mechanism: Choose-Your-Own-Disaster tabletop, monthly (scripts/hold-drill.py, scripts/_drills.py tabletop)
methods.measure: Every card in the scenario deck maps each required step to a section of the incident response runbook or the recovery plan, the plan states its recovery objectives, the after-action lessons resolve, and a planted card no runbook covers is flagged.

replaceable.statement: Real responders would play the same deck against the same runbooks; map_steps() and the after-action check would not change, only who reads the cards.

methods.mechanism: Vulnerability disclosure drill, monthly (scripts/hold-drill.py, scripts/_drills.py intake)
methods.measure: A report in the documented intake format is parsed, triaged, opens a finding and is acknowledged inside its clock, and a planted report with no reproduction steps is triaged to needs-info.

replaceable.statement: A real report's text would be passed to the same intake() in place of Ima Finder's; the transport that delivers it (today the security.txt contact) is what would change.

methods.mechanism: security.txt validity, every deploy (scripts/check-secure-config.py, in security-settings.json)
methods.measure: The published security.txt names a contact, the disclosure policy and its canonical URL, and expires in the future and within a year (RFC 9116).

methods.mechanism: Phishing drill, monthly (scripts/hold-drill.py, scripts/_phishing.py)
methods.measure: The lure's indicators are found by rule and none in a benign control message, the trainee's response is graded, a click assigns the remedial lesson of the training packet, and a planted click is graded a fail.

replaceable.statement: A real recipient's report or click (from a mail client's report button or the link's landing page) would replace respond(); detect() and grade() would not change. Nothing is sent today.

methods.mechanism: Nightly quarantine responder drill (scripts/_quarantine.py, run by scripts/audit-log-review.py)
methods.measure: A planted reportable event (Mallory McHypothetical (simulated), signed in from the Moon at 3 a.m. as a permissionless stand-in role) is caught by the audit-log rules, the responder attaches AWS's deny-all policy to the role it names, reads the deny back, removes it and reads the removal back, a planted request to quarantine a trust-root role is refused with no IAM call, and every real reportable event of the night was answered.

replaceable.statement: A real reportable finding that names an IAM user or role goes through the same quarantine() the drill calls, from respond(), on every nightly run; only the planted event and its stand-in role are simulated.

methods.mechanism: Monthly Chaos Gremlin restore drill (scripts/hold-chaos-gremlin.py)
methods.measure: Deployed site objects copied into a versioned scratch bucket are deleted and overwritten by the Chaos Gremlin (simulated), restored from their prior versions and read back identical to the deployed commit (sha256), with the measured restore time and restore-point age inside the recovery objectives of data/recovery-objectives.json and a planted forged restore caught.

methods.mechanism: Availability incidents measured against the recovery time objective (availability.json and data/recovery-objectives.json)
methods.measure: Every availability incident in the independent 30-day measurement, an ongoing one measured to now, lasted no longer than the recovery time objective.
